en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Dyad on the Tainted (Sāsavaduka)
Conditioned by a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive but with taints, there arises a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive and without taints, by way of root condition.

Conditioned by a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive but with taints, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive and without taints, by way of root condition. Conditioned by a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive but with taints...

Phenomena that are neither visible nor impinging and are not associated with taints, as well as phenomena that are neither visible nor impinging and are not associated with taints, arise by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Three [answers] for the root condition … pe … three for the non-disappearance condition.

Dependent on a phenomenon that is invisible, non-impinging, and not associated with taints, there arises a phenomenon that is neither invisible nor non-impinging and is not not associated with taints.
[An invisible and non-reactive state] arises with a root-condition. Dependent on an invisible, non-reactive, and untainted state,

there arises [a state that is] neither visible nor reactive and not untainted, with a root-condition …pe… Dependent on an invisible, non-reactive, and untainted state, there arise both [a state that is] neither visible nor reactive and not untainted, and [a state that is] neither visible nor reactive and untainted, with a root-condition.
Phenomena arise with root-condition as their condition. (Abbreviated. There are six [classes] for the root, six for the predominance … [and so on] … six for non-disappearance.
